title: Kenny Clarke and bringing along the young drummers
summary: Jones credits Kenny Clarke with Basie recordings credited to him and describes how veterans trained young drummers.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Now, we get back to Kansas - did you mention little Oliver, what's his name, that came to Cab's band?
We haven't talked about Kenny Clarke, Klook.
Kenny Clarke and I, practically the same age bracket. Kenny had a nice background in music - vibraphone, chimes, and tym and what have you. Matter of fact,
Kenny Clarke made some records with the Count Basie band and George Simon, who was a great fan of mine -

Yeh, amateur drummer, he would review the records and he wasn't in the studio and he said, "Jo Jones," and I said, "George, I wasn't there; that was Kenny Clarke." But Kenny would do what we were trying to do. We were trying to do something to bring these kids along and to try to help them, because we were already established and we already had a job, but who were we going to get for a replacement. Because you remember, Milt, in show business years ago when you got to be around 35 or 40 years old you stayed at home with your family and you went out and got another little kid to put in your place. It's time for you to quit traveling now; you're going to stay home and rear your family. When you have these things that couldn't be gotten out of a book - you can always go to an instructor. But how in the world could a kid's imagination be as keen as the experience that you had, and the experience was based upon mistakes. I used to give my Kenny my key to the Y. I said, "Take the kids up to the Y," because I belonged to the Businessman's Club. "Take them up there, work them out, let them swim, let them go through the gymnastics. If they did anything wrong just throw them down on a mat and choke them to death and say, 'Now you're not going to get

drunk Wednesday like you did last Wednesday. You better be on your job. Because you know good and well that Sid Catlett will come around and if you did anything wrong, we just get up and take your job."
